purpose: Compose recovered mesh allocation, descriptor history, direct integer buffers and boundary construction before integrating the keyword importer.
established_behavior: Node replacement clears and allocates coordinates, six direct integer buffers and 28 registered state variables; field 8 receives the supplied default.
Element replacement clears and allocates connectivity, direct integer buffer 61 and 25 registered state variables, preserving the recovered shape-history rules and field defaults.
Bulk replacement and row filling are separate operations, allowing partially imported arrays to remain visible after input failure.
Successful connectivity completion sets the mesh-present flag and invokes the recovered boundary builder. Coordinate replacement alone retains the previous boundary state.
The current internal API accepts explicit component controls and defaults rather than inferring scientific field meanings.

Mesh deactivation clears buffers and descriptor counts in place, retaining selected arity, descriptor width/multiplicity history and the active boundary-group count with empty payloads. Repeated deactivation updates previous counts to zero.

validation.qualification: The mesh-switching sequence combines previously used individual fixtures; its candidate was frozen before capture. The later populated-object deactivation capture supplies eight additional discovery snapshots and guided the new deactivate method. It is not held-out deactivation coverage.
validation.provenance: Independent verifier checks the new capture's four import statuses, 15 ordered events, 53 descriptor mappings per snapshot, pointer binding, buffer shapes and retained boundaries; 12 tampering cases are rejected.

design_choices: Portable vectors own storage. Native addresses, allocator behavior and physical object layout are not reproduced. The state comparator normalizes null buffers to empty arrays; it does not establish pointer-binding or allocation-identity equivalence.
Unsupported extents and multiplicities are rejected outside the established compatibility domain.
The replay fixture reader only supplies known test inputs; it is not the production keyword scanner.
remaining: Full object identity, names, types and cleanup outside the reconstructed mesh-owned portion.
Production keyword scanner, complete dispatch, status propagation and finalization. The integrated replay compares state and does not emit or compare importer return codes.
2D integrated allocation and dimension switching; the planar boundary component has separate comparisons.
Nondefault multiplicities, shared backing and copy/detach behavior.
Additional auxiliary and boundary-dependent arrays and derived scientific geometry.
Allocation failure, malformed indices, arbitrary mesh sizes and complete external ABI compatibility.
